correctness.rationale: RESULT.md lines 5–53 and 55–120. Rearrangement against the decreasing cosine on [0,π] gives |m|≤M and, by rotation, |c1|≤M. The stated u,v values stay in [0,π], enforce mass a, and integrate to the prescribed m and q. Subtracting the affine cosine/mass terms from cos 2θ gives exactly the quadratic sign certificate; integrating over the symmetric difference gives both identities and uniqueness because the zeros have measure zero, including the endpoints. The weak-* compact moment fiber in L∞ has an extreme point, and four positive-measure pieces suffice to contradict extremality of any density bounded away from 0 and 1 on a positive-measure subset; thus every interpolated pair is attained by an indicator. The width is 2M(1−m²/M²), giving area 8M²/3. Applying the real inequalities to both harmonics rotated together and maximizing the resulting second harmonic gives the disks with the stated signs and factors. Each equality forces one rotated set to be a real extremizer; symmetry makes its first coefficient real and rotation by π interchanges the ±r representatives. Both radii are positive for 0<a<1. The upper/lower sets give equality at every r, including zero and the one-arc endpoints. The sign convention in the proof can be read as rotation by −φ; it ranges over all angles. The packaged numerical code and output were inspected, not executed; the continuous proof decides correctness, and neither sufficiency of the two disks nor more Fourier modes is asserted.

Thus the true complex fiber is |c2−π cot(t)c1²|≤M−|c1|²/M, for |c1|≤M. The indexed phase-centred record treats first moments and two-cap concentration; the two-sided fixed-centre record treats bounded complex harmonic maps, not these strip fibers.

evidence: The two weaker disks follow by triangle inequality using γ−−γ+=π cot(t) and γ−+γ+=1/M. Projecting the exact fiber at c1=m+iy gives the stated bounds at y=0, with the upper envelope decreased by π cot(t/2)y² and lower envelope increased by π tan(t/2)y². The whole real lens follows by taking y=0. Its area is then direct integration.

Equality in projected bounds forces y=0 and Schur saturation, so the unique inverse-strip trace is an indicator supported on a preimage of a boundary semicircle under a degree-at-most-two Blaschke product (the split points need not form a semicircle in the coordinate W used here; the preimage is of a single boundary arc). This gives the one- or two-arc extremizers; the frozen endpoint formulas integrate those intervals. The deficit identity is the subtraction of equal linear constraints followed by sign partition.

The three frozen citations address arc mass reconstruction, recovery of a pre-specified union of arcs, and Hardy-space extremals for a fixed characteristic function, respectively; those particular passages do not supply the joint lens.
